questions.q: What is Harrow Peak Financial, as presented in this lesson?
options: An anonymized version of a real lawsuit
A real fintech startup mentioned in the EU AI Act
A real regional bank whose incident was reported in the news
A fictional company invented for this course's illustrative case study, not a real organization or incident
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly labels Harrow Peak Financial as fictional and illustrative, not a real company or incident.

questions.q: What specific data problem did the team discover during provenance review?
options: The model was trained on a competitor's data by mistake
The training data file was accidentally deleted
The data had no personal information in it at all
The historical training labels themselves already encoded a human bias from one branch's past lending pattern
questions.explain: The case study's key finding is that the 'ground truth' outcome labels already carried bias from a past human lending pattern, not a technical data-loss issue.

questions.q: Why did the drift-monitoring alert trigger a mandatory human review rather than a routine note in a ticket queue?
options: Because the model's accuracy score dropped to zero
Because the credit-decisioning system had been tiered high-risk from the start, which made that escalation path mandatory
Because the regulator had already opened an investigation
Because the company had unlimited engineering staff available that week
questions.explain: The high-risk tier assigned at the start (per Lesson 24's framework) is what made the mandatory human-review escalation automatic.

questions.q: According to the lesson, what did the team already know about fair-lending obligations before the model was ever built?
options: That fair-lending obligations only begin once a regulator issues a specific AI rule
That anti-discrimination and fair-lending duties around credit decisions already applied, regardless of whether an AI model made the call
That no legal obligations apply to lending decisions made by software
That fair-lending law only applies to human loan officers, never to software
questions.explain: The case study makes clear that fair-lending and anti-discrimination duties around credit decisions predate and apply regardless of whether a model or a human makes the call.

questions.q: What did the scheduled internal audit ultimately confirm in this case study?
options: That the model should be deleted immediately with no further use
That the audit itself was unnecessary and should be skipped next cycle
That the drift response was logged, escalated, and remediated correctly, demonstrating the governance program working in practice
That no governance controls had actually been followed
questions.explain: The audit (Lesson 27's mechanism) found the response was handled correctly end to end, confirming governance was real, not aspirational.
